features.title: Free Trial, Account Recovery, and One-Person Account Policy
features.what_you_see: A no-credit-card free trial tied to your verified account identity, followed by a non-destructive limited mode if the trial ends without a license.
what_it_looks_for: A verified account identity handled by the production authentication service
An existing trial/account record or a first-time trial claim
features.rigor: Account/trial/licensing state controls product capabilities only. It never changes scientific evidence, proof status, or stored experiment truth. Trial expiry never encrypts, corrupts, deletes, or holds user data hostage.
examples: Create your first account, start the free trial without entering a credit card, run experiments during the trial, then continue to view/export/delete your own work if the trial later expires.
If you return with the same verified identity, recover or merge the existing account rather than opening a second trial account; the original trial clock is preserved.

features.title: Self-Sandboxing Production Runtime
features.what_you_see: A webapp that starts the hardened CACE service layer with safe defaults and exposes only the web gateway to the client.
what_it_looks_for: Required local service permissions and writable data directories
Optional scientific/AI backends detected at startup
features.rigor: The browser remains untrusted presentation. Privileged science, AI, wallet, storage, network, and proof services stay behind the private service boundary and use least-privilege isolation. Missing optional backends degrade visibly instead of silently weakening verification.
examples: Start CACE on a supported machine and let the startup self-check initialize local data, validate service boundaries, and open the webapp without manual scientific configuration.
Run CACE without an optional GPU or local-AI provider; the affected capability reports unavailable/limited while ordinary supported experiments and evidence rules continue to work.
